questions.title: Sign not seen in dysthyroid eye disease
questions.question: The following are signs of dysthyroid (thyroid) eye disease EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it is a sign). Upper-lid retraction from sympathetic overactivity and muscle fibrosis is a classic sign of thyroid eye disease.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the exception: thyroid eye disease is an orbital and adnexal disorder (muscle and fat swelling) and does not inflame the uveal tract, so uveitis is not one of its signs. Uveitis points instead to an intraocular inflammatory cause. Hence uveitis is the odd one out.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it is a sign). Swelling of the extraocular muscles and orbital fat produces unilateral or bilateral proptosis.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it is a sign). Lid lag on downgaze (von Graefe sign) is a recognised feature.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that uveitis is not a sign of thyroid eye disease.

questions.title: Form that is not a type of dry eye
questions.question: Forms of dry eye include the following EXCEPT:

options.B: Mucin deficiency due to widespread loss of goblet cells

explanations.A: Incorrect (it is a form). Aqueous-tear deficiency (keratoconjunctivitis sicca) is the classic aqueous-deficient dry eye.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it is a form). Loss of goblet cells causes mucin-deficient dry eye with an unstable film.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it is a form). Eyelid disease that impairs blinking and tear spreading produces evaporative dry eye.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception: simple lid oedema swells the lid but does not reduce tear production or film stability, so it is not a recognised form of dry eye. The genuine forms reflect deficient aqueous, mucin or lipid, or impaired spreading. Hence lid oedema is the odd one out.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the true forms of dry eye from lid oedema.

questions.title: Gland involved in hordeolum externum (stye)
questions.question: Hordeolum externum (stye) is an acute inflammation of the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Although a stye is centred on a lash, the department answer localises the acute infection to the associated gland of Zeis rather than the follicle itself.
explanations.B: Correct. An external hordeolum (stye) is an acute staphylococcal abscess of a gland of Zeis at the base of an eyelash, presenting as a tender red swelling that points on the skin surface of the lid margin. It resolves with hot compresses, lid hygiene and sometimes epilation of the affected lash. Hence the stye is an inflammation of the gland of Zeis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The gland of Moll is the modified sweat gland; the stye is attributed here to the sebaceous gland of Zeis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The gland of Wolfring is an accessory lacrimal gland, not a lid-margin gland.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the stye as an acute infection of the gland of Zeis.

questions.title: Muscle paralysed in Horner's ptosis
questions.question: Ptosis in Horner's syndrome is due to paralysis of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Riolan's muscle is the marginal part of orbicularis and is not responsible for the Horner ptosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Horner's muscle is the lacrimal part of orbicularis, unrelated to lid elevation.
explanations.C: Correct. Horner's syndrome interrupts the ocular sympathetic supply and so paralyses Muller's muscle (the smooth superior tarsal muscle), giving a mild ptosis. The striated levator palpebrae superioris, supplied by the oculomotor nerve, remains intact, which is why the ptosis is only slight. Hence the ptosis is due to Muller's-muscle paralysis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Levator paralysis is a third-nerve problem and causes a much greater ptosis than that of Horner's syndrome.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute Horner's ptosis to sympathetic denervation of Muller's muscle.

questions.title: Feature of squamous blepharitis
questions.question: In squamous blepharitis:

options.A: The lid margin is not inflamed.
options.B: Scaly dandruff-like material is seen between the cilia.
options.D: It causes ulcers on the lid margin.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The lid margin is chronically inflamed and hyperaemic in squamous blepharitis.
explanations.B: Correct. Squamous (seborrhoeic) blepharitis is a chronic inflammation of the lid margin characterised by dry, scaly dandruff-like material clinging between the lashes. Unlike ulcerative blepharitis it does not produce hard crusts or bleeding ulcers, and it is managed with lid hygiene. Hence scaly dandruff-like material between the cilia is its hallmark.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It is not a fungal disease; treatment is lid hygiene, not antifungals.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ulcers on the lid margin belong to ulcerative (staphylococcal) blepharitis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the scales of squamous (seborrhoeic) blepharitis.

questions.title: Cause of congenital ptosis
questions.question: Congenital ptosis is due to:

options.A: Increased weight of the upper lid

explanations.A: Incorrect. Increased lid weight (mechanical ptosis) is an acquired, not a congenital, mechanism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Levator tendon (aponeurotic) injury causes acquired ptosis, typically after trauma or surgery.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A third-nerve palsy is a neurogenic acquired cause, usually with other ocular motility signs.
explanations.D: Correct. Congenital ptosis results from a developmental dystrophy of the levator palpebrae superioris, in which the muscle is maldeveloped and partly replaced by fibro-fatty tissue. Because the dystrophic muscle also relaxes poorly, there is lid lag on downgaze. Hence congenital ptosis is due to dystrophy of the levator muscle.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute congenital ptosis to a dystrophic levator muscle.

questions.title: Condition that does not cause proptosis
questions.question: Proptosis is present in the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it causes proptosis). Orbital cellulitis increases orbital volume with inflammatory swelling and pushes the globe forward.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it causes proptosis). Cavernous sinus thrombosis obstructs orbital venous drainage, producing congestion and proptosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it causes proptosis). Extraocular muscle and fat swelling in thyroid eye disease is the commonest cause of adult proptosis.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception: acute angle-closure glaucoma raises the intraocular pressure and gives a red, painful eye, but it does not increase orbital volume and so does not push the globe forward. Proptosis reflects an orbital, not an intraocular-pressure, problem. Hence acute angle-closure glaucoma does not cause proptosis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that acute angle-closure glaucoma does not cause proptosis.

questions.title: Cause that does not produce ptosis
questions.question: Ptosis can occur due to the following causes EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it causes ptosis). Congenital weakness of the levator muscle is a classic cause of ptosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it causes ptosis). Lid trauma can disinsert the levator aponeurosis and produce aponeurotic ptosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it causes ptosis). Third-nerve palsy denervates the levator and causes a marked ptosis.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception: the orbicularis oculi CLOSES the lid, so its paralysis causes incomplete closure (lagophthalmos) and lower-lid ectropion, not drooping. Lid elevation, and therefore ptosis, depends on the levator and Muller's muscle. Hence orbicularis paralysis does not cause ptosis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that orbicularis paralysis causes lagophthalmos, not ptosis.

questions.title: Diagnostic use of Schirmer's test
questions.question: Schirmer's test is used for diagnosing:

explanations.A: Correct. The Schirmer test measures aqueous tear production from the length of wetting of a filter-paper strip placed in the lower fornix over five minutes. Reduced wetting indicates an aqueous-deficient dry eye. Hence Schirmer's test is used to diagnose dry eye.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Infective keratitis is diagnosed by slit-lamp examination and corneal scrapes, not Schirmer's test.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Corneal ulcers are demonstrated by fluorescein staining, not by measuring tear volume.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Horner's syndrome is assessed by pupil examination and pharmacological testing.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Schirmer's test as a measure of tear production in dry eye.

questions.title: Commonest cause of unilateral proptosis in adults
questions.question: The most common cause of adult unilateral proptosis is:

explanations.A: Correct. Thyroid (Graves) orbitopathy is the commonest cause of proptosis in adults, whether unilateral or bilateral, because the autoimmune swelling of the extraocular muscles and orbital fat is often asymmetrical. It therefore heads the differential for a single protruding eye in an adult. Hence thyroid orbitopathy is the commonest cause of adult unilateral proptosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Orbital metastasis is an uncommon cause of unilateral proptosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Orbital lymphoma is much less common than thyroid disease.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A sphenoid-wing meningioma can cause unilateral proptosis but is far rarer than thyroid orbitopathy.

questions.learning_objective: Identify thyroid orbitopathy as the commonest cause of adult proptosis, unilateral or bilateral.

questions.title: Source of the mucin layer of tears
questions.question: The mucin layer of tears is secreted by:

explanations.A: Correct. The innermost mucin layer of the pre-corneal tear film is secreted by conjunctival goblet cells. It wets the naturally hydrophobic corneal epithelium so that the aqueous layer can spread evenly, and its loss (for example in vitamin A deficiency) destabilises the tear film. Hence the mucin layer is secreted by goblet cells.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The main lacrimal gland secretes the middle aqueous layer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The meibomian glands secrete the outer lipid layer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The accessory lacrimal glands add to the aqueous, not the mucin, layer.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute the tear-film mucin layer to conjunctival goblet cells.

questions.title: Drainage site of the nasolacrimal duct
questions.question: The nasolacrimal duct opens in the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior meatus receives the posterior ethmoidal sinuses, not the nasolacrimal duct.
explanations.B: Correct. Tears drain from the lacrimal sac down the nasolacrimal duct, which opens into the inferior nasal meatus beneath the inferior turbinate. This anatomy explains why the nose runs during crying and guides syringing and dacryocystorhinostomy. Hence the nasolacrimal duct opens in the inferior nasal meatus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The middle meatus drains the frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoidal sinuses.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity, not directly into the nasopharynx.

questions.learning_objective: State that the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior nasal meatus.

questions.title: Differentiating a stye from a chalazion
questions.question: You can differentiate between a stye and a chalazion by:

options.A: The relation of the lesion to the caruncle
options.B: The relation to the lid margin

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neither lesion is defined by its relation to the caruncle.
explanations.B: Correct. A stye (external hordeolum) arises from a gland of Zeis at the lash line and points at the lid margin, whereas a chalazion is a meibomian-gland granuloma that sits within the tarsal plate away from the margin. Their position relative to the lid margin is therefore what distinguishes them. Hence relation to the lid margin differentiates the two.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The amount of discharge is not a reliable discriminator between them.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Everting the lid helps display a chalazion but is not the defining difference.

questions.learning_objective: Differentiate a stye from a chalazion by position relative to the lid margin.

questions.title: Gland involved in a chalazion
questions.question: A chalazion is a chronic inflammatory granuloma of the:

explanations.A: Correct. A chalazion is a chronic, sterile, lipogranulomatous inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland within the tarsal plate. It presents as a painless firm nodule set back from the lid margin and is treated by incision and curettage if it persists. Hence a chalazion is a granuloma of a meibomian gland.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Acute infection of the gland of Zeis is an external hordeolum (stye), not a chalazion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The gland of Moll is the modified sweat gland of the lid margin and is not the seat of a chalazion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The gland of Wolfring is an accessory lacrimal gland.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the chalazion as a meibomian-gland granuloma.

questions.title: Treatment of severe ptosis with no levator function
questions.question: Severe congenital ptosis with no levator function can be treated by:

options.A: Levator resection from the skin side
options.B: Surgical intervention between the age of 6 and 10 years

explanations.A: Incorrect. Levator resection needs some residual levator function to work and fails when the muscle is absent.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Severe ptosis covering the pupil is repaired early to prevent amblyopia, not deferred to age 6-10.
explanations.C: Correct. When levator function is absent, lid elevation is transferred to the frontalis muscle by a frontalis (brow) suspension sling, so the patient raises the lid with the eyebrow. This is the standard procedure for ptosis with poor or no levator action. Hence a frontalis sling is used.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tarsorrhaphy narrows the fissure to protect the cornea and does not correct ptosis.

questions.learning_objective: Select the frontalis sling for ptosis with absent levator function.

questions.title: Incorrect statement about incomplete lid closure in sleep
questions.question: If the palpebral fissure does not close completely during sleep, choose the WRONG answer:

options.B: There is usually trigeminal nerve palsy.
options.C: Bell's phenomenon protects the cornea from ulceration.
options.D: Lateral tarsorrhaphy is one of the management lines.

explanations.A: Incorrect (this is a true statement). Incomplete lid closure is by definition lagophthalmos.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the wrong statement: lid closure is driven by orbicularis oculi, supplied by the FACIAL (7th) nerve, so lagophthalmos follows facial-nerve palsy, not trigeminal palsy. The trigeminal nerve is sensory to the cornea and does not move the lids. Hence attributing the condition to trigeminal palsy is incorrect.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this is a true statement). Bell's phenomenon rolls the globe up on attempted closure and shields the cornea.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this is a true statement). Lateral tarsorrhaphy narrows the fissure and is a recognised treatment for exposure.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that lagophthalmos follows facial, not trigeminal, nerve palsy.

questions.title: Investigation that is not a test for dry eye
questions.question: One of the following is NOT a test for dry eye:

explanations.A: Correct. The Hirschberg corneal-reflex test estimates ocular alignment (the angle of strabismus) and has nothing to do with tear function. Tests for dry eye instead measure tear volume, ocular-surface damage or tear composition. Hence the Hirschberg test is not a dry-eye test.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Rose bengal stains devitalised, poorly wetted epithelium and is a recognised dry-eye test.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Schirmer's test measures aqueous tear production.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A reduced tear lysozyme level reflects lacrimal hyposecretion in dry eye.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish dry-eye tests from the Hirschberg strabismus test.

questions.title: Consequence not caused by defective lacrimal drainage
questions.question: Defective lacrimal drainage can result in any of these conditions EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it is a consequence). Stagnant tears in an obstructed sac become infected, giving chronic dacryocystitis.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the exception: trichiasis is an inward misdirection of the eyelashes from lid-margin disease and has nothing to do with tear drainage. The genuine drainage-obstruction sequelae are infection, sac distension and punctal changes. Hence trichiasis is the odd one out.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it is a consequence). Chronic stagnation and inflammation can narrow and stenose the puncti.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it is a consequence). A blocked, distended, mucus-filled sac forms a mucocele.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that trichiasis is not a sequela of lacrimal drainage obstruction.

questions.title: Clinical features of congenital ptosis
questions.question: Congenital ptosis is characterised by:

explanations.A: Incorrect as the single answer. An absent or poorly formed lid crease does occur, but it is only one of several features.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the single answer. A compensatory chin-up head posture does occur, but it is not the whole picture.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the single answer. Forehead corrugation from frontalis overaction does occur, but again it is only one feature.
explanations.D: Correct. Congenital ptosis from a dystrophic levator shows a poorly formed or absent upper-lid crease, a compensatory chin-up head posture to see under the drooping lid, and forehead corrugation as the frontalis is recruited to lift the lid. All three features are therefore present. Hence the answer is all of the above.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the clinical triad of congenital ptosis.

questions.title: Treatment not used for hordeolum internum
questions.question: Treatment of hordeolum internum includes all of the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it is used). Hot fomentation relieves pain and encourages the abscess to point and drain.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it is used). Topical or systemic antibiotics treat the staphylococcal infection.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it is used). If the abscess points, incision and evacuation release the pus.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception: an internal hordeolum is an abscess of a tarsal MEIBOMIAN gland, which has no associated eyelash, so there is no related lash to epilate. Lash epilation belongs to the treatment of an external stye. Hence epilation is not part of managing an internal hordeolum.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that lash epilation does not treat an internal hordeolum.

questions.title: Cause of trichiasis
questions.question: Trichiasis is caused by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Angular blepharitis inflames the outer canthus but does not scar the lash line to misdirect the lashes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An internal hordeolum is a self-limiting meibomian abscess and does not cause lash misdirection.
explanations.C: Correct. Trichiasis is an inward misdirection of the eyelashes against the globe and follows cicatricial lid-margin disease. Chronic ulcerative (staphylococcal) blepharitis scars the lash line and turns the lashes inward. Hence ulcerative blepharitis causes trichiasis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The follicular (active) stage of trachoma has not yet scarred the conjunctiva; it is the later cicatricial stage of trachoma, not follicular trachoma, that produces trichiasis.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute trichiasis to the lid-margin scarring of ulcerative blepharitis.

questions.title: Cause that does not produce dry eye
questions.question: Dry eye can be caused by all of the following EXCEPT:

options.C: Atrophy of the accessory lacrimal glands

explanations.A: Correct. This is the exception: obstruction of the lacrimal puncti blocks tear DRAINAGE, so tears accumulate and the eye WATERS (epiphora) rather than becoming dry. Dry eye instead reflects deficient tear production or an unstable film. Hence punctal obstruction does not cause dry eye.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it causes dry eye). Collagen vascular diseases such as Sjögren's syndrome destroy the lacrimal gland and reduce tear secretion.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it causes dry eye). Atrophy of the accessory lacrimal glands lowers basal tear production.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it causes dry eye). Vitamin A deficiency causes goblet-cell loss, conjunctival keratinisation and an unstable tear film.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish tear-deficiency causes of dry eye from punctal (drainage) obstruction.

questions.title: Structure not part of the lacrimal secretory system
questions.question: The lacrimal secretory system consists of the following parts EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it is secretory). The main lacrimal gland secretes the aqueous layer of reflex tears.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it is secretory). The accessory lacrimal glands of Krause and Wolfring provide basal tear secretion.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it is secretory). Conjunctival goblet cells secrete the mucin layer of the tear film.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception: the lacrimal sac belongs to the excretory (drainage) apparatus that carries tears from the puncti and canaliculi to the nasolacrimal duct, not to the tear-secreting system. The secretory system is the glands and goblet cells. Hence the lacrimal sac is the odd one out.

questions.learning_objective: Separate the secretory glands from the draining lacrimal sac.

questions.title: Function of the orbital portion of the lacrimal gland
questions.question: The orbital portion of the lacrimal gland is responsible for:

explanations.A: Correct. The main (orbital and palpebral) lacrimal gland produces reflex tears in response to ocular irritation or emotion. Basal, resting secretion comes mainly from the accessory lacrimal glands of Krause and Wolfring. Hence the orbital portion of the lacrimal gland is responsible for reflex tear secretion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Basal tear secretion is largely the job of the accessory lacrimal glands.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The mucin layer is secreted by conjunctival goblet cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The orbital lacrimal gland has a definite role, namely reflex tear secretion.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute reflex tear secretion to the main lacrimal gland.

questions.title: Meaning of a positive regurgitation test
questions.question: A positive regurgitation test is diagnostic of:

explanations.A: Correct. In the regurgitation test, pressure over the lacrimal sac refluxes mucoid or mucopurulent material back through the punctum. A positive result means the canaliculus is patent but the nasolacrimal duct is blocked, so fluid has accumulated in the sac (chronic dacryocystitis). Hence a positive regurgitation test indicates nasolacrimal duct obstruction.
explanations.B: Incorrect. In canalicular obstruction the passage to the sac is blocked, so nothing can reflux and the test is negative.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Punctal occlusion prevents fluid from re-emerging at the punctum, so no regurgitation is seen.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ectropion causes watering from lid malposition and does not give sac regurgitation.

questions.learning_objective: Interpret a positive regurgitation test as nasolacrimal duct obstruction.
